set system host-name [parameter1].explanation: Configure the host name of the device.

parameters.name: hostname
parameters.explanation: The host name of the equipment is used to identify the equipment in the network.

unit [parameter2].explanation: Configure the unit number of the interface.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.explanation: Interface unit numbers that distinguish between multiple logical configurations under the same interface.

family inet address [parameter3]/[parame.explanation: Configure IPv4 addresses for interfaces and subnet masks.

parameters.name: ip-address
parameters.explanation: The IPv4 address assigned to the interface.

parameters.name: autonomous-system
parameters.explanation: Autonomy system number for equipment, used for route agreements such as BGP.

parameters.name: prefix-list
parameters.explanation: The name of the prefix list.

set policy-options community [parameter1.explanation: The command `set policy-options community [parameter1]` defines a new BGP community with the name or value specified by `[parameter1]` for route tagging and policy control.

members [parameter2].explanation: Configure community members in the strategy options.

set policy-options policy-statement [par.explanation: This command fragment defines a routing policy named `[parameter1]` in Junos, allowing you to configure specific routing rules, actions, and conditions for traffic control.

term [parameter2].explanation: This command fragment configures a routing policy by defining a term within a policy statement, where `[parameter1]` is the policy name and `[parameter2]` is the term name.

parameters.name: term
parameters.explanation: The term number of the policy statement.

from prefix-list [parameter3].explanation: Configures the list of prefixes for which the policy statement matches.

parameters.name: prefix-list
parameters.explanation: The name or specific prefix of the prefix list.

then community add [parameter3].explanation: The command `then community add [parameter3]` in Junos adds the specified BGP community value (`[parameter3]`) to the route's existing community attributes.

parameters.name: community-name
parameters.explanation: The name of the community attribute.

then accept.explanation: Configure the action of the policy statement as accepted.

from route-filter [parameter3]/[paramete.explanation: This command fragment configures a routing policy to match routes based on a specific prefix (`parameter3`) and prefix length (`parameter4`) within a defined term (`parameter2`) of a policy statement (`parameter1`).

parameters.name: route-filter
parameters.explanation: Route filter, specify a matching route prefix.

parameters.name: prefix-length
parameters.explanation: The length of the route prefix.

exact.explanation: Configures the matching conditions for the policy statement, which accurately matches the given route.

then reject.explanation: The command `then reject` in Junos drops the matching traffic and sends an ICMP unreachable message back to the source.

set protocols bgp group [parameter1].explanation: This command configures a BGP group named [parameter1], defining a set of BGP peers with shared session parameters.

type [parameter2].explanation: Configure the type of BGP group to be external.

parameters.name: type
parameters.explanation: Type of BGP group, for example, external.

local-address [parameter2].explanation: Configure the local address of the BGP group.

parameters.name: local-address
parameters.explanation: Local address of the BGP group.

peer-as [parameter2].explanation: The equivalent autonomy system number for BGP groups.

neighbor [parameter2].explanation: Configure the neighbors of the BGP team.

family inet unicast.explanation: Configure BGP teams to support IPv4 solo addresses.

multihop ttl [parameter2].explanation: The command `multihop ttl [parameter2]` sets the Time-To-Live (TTL) value for BGP multihop sessions, controlling the maximum number of hops for BGP packets.

set protocols ospf area [parameter1].explanation: This command configures an OSPF area in Junos OS, where `[parameter1]` specifies the area ID, enabling OSPF routing within the defined area.

interface [parameter2].explanation: Configure interfaces in the OSPF area.

passive.explanation: Configure the interface in the OSPF area as passive mode.
